title: Troubleshoot a Haas mill spindle before replacing it
scope: Spindle symptom troubleshooting as demonstrated in SRC_HAAS_0009.

context.subsystem: mill spindle (lubrication, heat, noise/vibration, tool sticking)

machine_family.note: The official description speaks of 'your mill spindle'.

subsystem.note: Named in the title and narration.

symptoms.note: The four symptoms are stated in the narration and shown as on-screen headings.

context.text: The presenter says a spindle is all too often replaced without finding the root cause, which leads to another failure down the road.

action.text: The presenter says to stop and do some troubleshooting to rule out other issues before going to the trouble of replacing the spindle.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

outcome.text: The presenter says that with a little troubleshooting there is a good chance the problem can be solved and the machine back up and running.

questions.question: How do you confirm the root cause is found before deciding to replace the spindle?

steps.title: Seized spindle: check lubrication and the pump

condition.text: The presenter starts from a spindle that has seized and quit running.

rationale.text: The presenter says most often the root cause is lubrication, meaning the spindle is not getting enough oil.
The presenter says pumps can work intermittently as they age, so even a successful lube test is no guarantee that the pump is good.
rationale.explanation: The captions state this directly. Cue 6 is corrected from 'busier pump' to 'Bijur pump' (the on-screen overlay reads 'CHECK THE BIJUR PUMP').

rationale.text: The presenter says that if any of these problems are not corrected, the new spindle will seize just like the old one.

action.text: The presenter says to pay particular attention to the pump if the machine has a Bijur pump.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The overlay 'LUBRICATION - CHECK THE BIJUR PUMP' appears over the presenter, who sits beside a white cabinet.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Overlay 'LUBRICATION - CHECK THE BIJUR PUMP' over the presenter, who sits beside a white cabinet.
evidence.explanation: The overlay text is legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about a Bijur pump.

action.text: The presenter says these pumps should always be rebuilt when a spindle problem is suspected, and that a rebuild is necessary anyway if the pump is over five years old.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The presenter says to switch older pump oils out for the current spec oils, either Mobil SHC 625 or a high quality synthetic 5W-20 automotive-type oil, both of which are direct replacements.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The two older oils are garbled in the captions and are deliberately not named. Cue 11 is corrected from 'Mobil SH c6 25' to 'Mobil SHC 625' (the on-screen parts page reads 'OIL, REFILL MOBIL SHC 625').

action.text: A Haas parts page for 'OIL, REFILL MOBIL SHC 625', part number 93-2220A, is shown with the overlay 'ALWAYS USE'.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Haas parts page for 'OIL, REFILL MOBIL SHC 625', part 93-2220A, with the overlay 'ALWAYS USE'.
evidence.explanation: The product title, part number and overlay are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about the current spec oils.

action.text: The presenter says that for a metering-valve-style pump the user should check for air leaks and bubbles inside the tank at the bottom of the valve body, and in the tube that carries oil into the sight glass.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The pump brand before 'metering valve' is garbled in the caption and is not repeated.

action.text: The overlay 'LUBRICATION - CHECK THE VALVE BODY' appears over a close-up of a reservoir with MIN and MAX marks.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Overlay 'LUBRICATION - CHECK THE VALVE BODY' over a close-up of a Bijur Delimon reservoir with MIN/MAX marks.
evidence.explanation: The overlay text and the reservoir markings are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about checking air in the valve body tank.

action.text: The presenter says to check for oil leaks at the sight glass.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

observation.text: The presenter says that if air bubbles can be seen, the pump is not properly lubricating the spindle.
The presenter says that if oil is leaking at the sight glass, the spindle is not being properly lubricated.

questions.question: How is the pump rebuild or oil change confirmed as having fixed the lubrication?

steps.title: Spindle running hot: check the amount of oil

condition.text: The presenter turns to a spindle that is running hot.

rationale.text: The presenter says the most common reason for a hot spindle is too much oil reaching the spindle.

action.text: The presenter says to check the lubrication system and make sure the proper amount of oil is being delivered.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The presenter says the procedure varies by machine model and pump type, and to refer to the pump documentation and follow its procedure.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The web address is garbled in the caption; the on-screen overlay reads 'REFER TO DIY.HAASCNC.COM'.

action.text: The overlay 'OVERHEATING - TOO MUCH OIL - PROPER AMOUNT OF OIL' appears over a lubrication reservoir with MIN and MAX marks, behind an open door.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Overlay 'OVERHEATING - TOO MUCH OIL - PROPER AMOUNT OF OIL' over a lubrication reservoir with MIN/MAX marks, behind an open door.
evidence.explanation: The overlay lines are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about delivering the proper amount of oil.

outcome.text: The presenter says fixing this will most likely correct the problem and save replacing the spindle.

questions.question: What oil amount or delivery rate is correct? The video defers to the pump documentation.

steps.title: Noise or vibration: rule out tooling, balance, alignment and belts

condition.text: The presenter turns to a spindle with a noise or vibration problem.

action.text: The presenter says to check that the tooling is not the problem and that the spindle is balanced properly before replacing the spindle.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The presenter says to make sure the spindle and motor are properly aligned.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly. The caption puts 'on an inline spindle' just before this sentence, so it is not clear whether it limits the alignment check or only the balancing video; the claim leaves it out.

action.text: The presenter says that if the spindle is belt driven, to make sure the belt tension is correct and the belts and sprockets are clean and in good condition.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The overlay 'NOISE/VIBRATION - CHECK YOUR TOOLING - SPINDLE IS BALANCED - CHECK ALIGNMENT / TENSION' appears beside the presenter holding a tool.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Overlay 'NOISE/VIBRATION - CHECK YOUR TOOLING - SPINDLE IS BALANCED - CHECK ALIGNMENT / TENSION' beside the presenter holding a tool.
evidence.explanation: The three overlay lines are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about balance, alignment and belt tension.

context.text: The presenter says a video covers the balancing procedure for an inline spindle, and that the alignment check is also covered in the spindle balancing video.

questions.question: What balance or vibration reading counts as acceptable?
Does the alignment check apply only to inline spindles, or to every spindle with a separate motor?

steps.title: Stuck tool: check tooling, application and spindle temperature

condition.text: The presenter turns to a spindle where the tool is sticking.

observation.text: The presenter says that with a stuck tool the spindle is rarely the problem, and it is much more likely to be about the tools used and the application.

rationale.text: The presenter says really long or heavy tools can lead to the tool fretting in the taper.
The presenter says tools are more likely to stick in a hot spindle.

action.text: The presenter says to take a careful look at any applications using long or heavy tools to make sure they are not contributing to the problem.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The presenter says to go back and look at the spindle temperature again, and to deal with the lubrication problem described earlier.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

action.text: The overlay 'STUCK TOOL - CHECK TOOLING / APPLICATION - CHECK LONG TOOLS - CHECK SPINDLE TEMPERATURE' appears over the presenter.

attribution.label: D1-A keyframe observation, pending human check

evidence.observation_note: Overlay 'STUCK TOOL - CHECK TOOLING / APPLICATION - CHECK LONG TOOLS - CHECK SPINDLE TEMPERATURE' over the presenter.
evidence.explanation: The overlay lines are legible in the frame.

action.explanation: The narration at this moment is about spindle temperature and the lubrication problem.

outcome.text: The presenter says dealing with the lubrication problem will probably solve the tool sticking problem as well.

steps.title: Correct orientation damage before replacing the spindle

condition.text: The presenter says this applies if the drive dogs or the spindle taper have been damaged by an orientation problem.

action.text: The presenter says the orientation problem must be corrected before the spindle is replaced.
action.explanation: The captions state this directly.

questions.question: How is the orientation problem diagnosed and corrected? The video only says it must be corrected.

claim.text: The presenter moves from the general advice to troubleshooting by symptom, starting with a spindle that has seized.
The presenter moves on to a spindle that is running hot.
The presenter next considers a spindle with a noise or vibration problem.
The presenter finally considers a spindle where the tool is sticking.
The presenter adds one last note about spindle damage caused by an orientation problem.
